beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Artificial intelligence can produce candidate research faster than institutions can validate it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Frontier Is Correction asks what scientific progress means under that reversal.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: More hypotheses and polished reports do not by themselves establish more knowledge.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book proposes a research programme organized around finding and acting on error.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its distinctive question is whether reality can still force an automated process to change.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You will encounter technical architecture alongside the institutional authority needed to govern it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This introduction explains why that combination deserves a researcher's attention.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The introduction follows a plausible claim arriving before its supporting evidence is secure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A fluent explanation can hide a weak baseline, contamination or a causal mistake.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The problem is not that every machine-generated candidate is worthless.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It is that a candidate and an accepted claim occupy different scientific positions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book uses that gap to organize the layers an inquiry needs.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Each layer should expose a failure that polished prose might otherwise conceal.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading starts with a familiar research difficulty before widening toward the proposed infrastructure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The philosophical opening treats science as a changing social technology for criticism.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A claim's formal vulnerability is not enough if nobody can force its revision.
